input.quote: 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
input.rationale: Section 13.1, the grant for the subscription Services, is walk-away territory: it runs to "Customer alone", expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them, is non-transferable, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion. Sections 13.2 and 13.3 give us the preferred position for the paid-up software licence (perpetual, irrevocable, Affiliates and contractor support) and a transfer right to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24 (which under 24.1 includes a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent), but 13.1 contradicts those protections for the Services licence. The single edit to 13.1 extends the grant to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf and replaces at-will revocation with the uncured material breach standard already in 13.3, and deleting "non-transferable" removes the conflict with the 13.3 transfer right. No separate personnel or access clause prohibits contractor use, so no collateral change is needed.

proposal.summary: Extend the Services licence in 13.1 to Affiliates and contractors and remove Vendor's at-will revocation and the non-transferability bar.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a Services licence granted to Meridian alone that Copperleaf may revoke at will, so we have extended the grant to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf and tied revocation to the uncured material breach standard already in Section 13.3 (which also preserves our transfer rights to an Affiliate or successor).
